paths.title: Beginner
paths.summary: Learn the lifecycle spine, the quality lenses you will use immediately, and enough master-data vocabulary to follow the journey without getting lost.
paths.outcome: You can place a customer or a product on the seven stages, name a quality defect by its dimension, and explain why a system of record matters.

steps.note: Why a map beats a pile of keywords.
Translate UW, NIST RDaF, and USGS without picking a fight about labels.
The seven-stage spine this site uses everywhere else.
Context and standards at the door.
Custody, backups, and the system of record.
Six ways data fails a decision.
From a dimension to a monitor and a source fix.
What master data is, in one domain you can picture.

paths.title: Practitioner
paths.audience: Analysts, stewards, and engineers who already know the lifecycle
paths.summary: Walk the DAMA wheel as actual work, then the roles and the MDM mechanics you will operate: golden records, match and merge, hierarchies.
paths.outcome: You can say what each knowledge area owes the others, assign a RACI without theater, and describe a merge you could also undo.

steps.note: The hub, and what it refuses to let other areas invent.
Blueprints and rival systems of record.
Service levels, restores, retirement of stores.
The unstructured half of the truth.
Where reference and master sit on the wheel.
Fit for use as a loop, not a cleanse.
Rollups that do not rewrite history.

paths.title: Governance lead
paths.audience: People standing up decision rights, a council, or a stewardship rhythm
paths.summary: Policies, forums, metrics, risk translation, and the day-2 MDM operation a sponsor will ask you to show.
paths.outcome: You can charter a thin governance system, map a principle to a control, and run a queue that proves the system is alive.

steps.note: Principles become controls. Not legal advice.
Publish the matrix where the request happens.
